question_en:
I am organizing the file for a used racing vehicle and verifying the race dispute records and engine spare part numbers left by the previous owner. Attached is a track map, and there is also a note in the folder that reads "2014 parts catalogue". Please answer the following questions:
1. Which racetrack is shown in the image? Which race does it correspond to? Please provide the race name, round or race number, and the date held.
2. Find the final appeal ruling on the camshaft dispute at this event, and provide the case number, ruling date, and ruling result; also provide the brand and part number of the standard camshaft used for comparison during the inspection.
3. Based on the standard camshaft number and the 2014 catalogue clue, confirm the corresponding vehicle model and find the original factory parts diagram for this model. What is the part number in the 2014 catalogue for the timing chain tensioner to the right of gasket No. 7 in the diagram? What are the two other early OEM numbers that can be used interchangeably?

Answer format: Please answer in points numbered (1)–(3). Each point should only answer the corresponding sub-question and provide all information required by that question.
answer:
(1) Racetrack: Motorsport Arena Oschersleben; Race: Round 7 of the 2025 FIM Sidecar World Championship, IMN 105/07; Date: October 3–5, 2025.

(2) Case number: FIM International Court of Appeal CAI-2025-03; Ruling date: February 4, 2026; Result: Appeal dismissed, disqualification decision upheld; Standard camshaft brand: Yamaha; Part number: 13S-12170-01 (full order number 13S-12170-01-00).

(3) Corresponding model: 2014 Yamaha YZF-R6; Original factory parts diagram: FIG. 4 CAMSHAFT & CHAIN; Tensioner number in the 2014 catalogue: 13S-12210-01-00; Two interchangeable early OEM numbers: 13S-12210-00-00, 2C0-12210-00-00.

## Step 01 · Deconstruct the prompt and establish fields to verify

**Action:** Record required fields for each sub-question according to the current prompt; first identify bridge entities from the input image, then map each answer field to verifiable sources.

**Evidence Observation:**

1. Which racetrack is shown in the image? Which race does it correspond to? Please provide the race name, round or race number, and the date held.
2. Find the final appeal ruling on the camshaft dispute at this event, and provide the case number, ruling date, and ruling result; also provide the brand and part number of the standard camshaft used for comparison during the inspection.
3. Based on the standard camshaft number and the 2014 catalogue clue, confirm the corresponding vehicle model and find the original factory parts diagram for this model. What is the part number in the 2014 catalogue for the timing chain tensioner to the right of gasket No. 7 in the diagram? What are the two other early OEM numbers that can be used interchangeably?

Answer format: Please answer in points numbered (1)–(3). Each point should only answer the corresponding sub-question and provide all information required by that question.

**Result of this step:** The retrieval path expands according to these sub-questions; the image is responsible for the object entry point, while numbers, dates, statistics, and status must be read from corresponding records.

## Step 02 · Establish candidates from the anonymous track map

**Action:** Observe clockwise direction, turns 1–14, start/finish line, and timing point layout; example query: Oschersleben circuit map camshaft appeal.

**Evidence Observation:**

The track map itself supports comparison of the circuit outline, but the whiteboard scene does not give the event year. First identify Oschersleben as a candidate, then use “camshaft appeal” to narrow down the relevant event. Do not treat the 2025 sidecar event as information already visible in the input.

**Evidence Link:**

https://www.fim-moto.com/fileadmin/user_upload/Documents/2025/2025_FIM_Sidecar_WC_-_Supplementary_Regulations_-_R7_Oschersleben.pdf
https://www.fim-moto.com/en/news/news-detail/article/update-following-fim-sidecar-world-championship-round-7

**Result of this step:** The candidate venue points to Motorsport Arena Oschersleben.

## Step 03 · Verify graphics against official supplementary regulations

**Action:** Read Annex 1 track map from the FIM Supplementary Regulations and compare the corner and direction layout.

**Evidence Observation:**

Official documents bind the same layout to Oschersleben, Germany; the homepage event is the 2025 FIM Sidecar World Championship Round 7. The figure and text belong to the same PDF; image matching provides the identity bridge, while race fields still need to be checked in the main text.

**Evidence Link:**

https://www.fim-moto.com/fileadmin/user_upload/Documents/2025/2025_FIM_Sidecar_WC_-_Supplementary_Regulations_-_R7_Oschersleben.pdf

**Result of this step:** The venue and race category receive support from official documents.

## Step 04 · Transcribe the unique identifier for this event

**Action:** Read the race number and date from the same PDF; do not substitute other Oschersleben events from the calendar.

**Evidence Observation:**

Race number IMN105/07, date 2025-10-03 to 2025-10-05, Round 7. These three fields jointly limit subsequent searches to prevent technical cases from other years at the same racetrack from being mixed in.

**Evidence Link:**

https://www.fim-moto.com/fileadmin/user_upload/Documents/2025/2025_FIM_Sidecar_WC_-_Supplementary_Regulations_-_R7_Oschersleben.pdf

**Result of this step:** Compose the query key Oschersleben＋105/07＋Round 7.

## Step 05 · Locate the technical incident and appeal entry point

**Action:** Example query: site:fim-moto.com Oschersleben Round 7 Team Steinhausen camshafts appeal.

**Evidence Observation:**

Official updates record post-race engine inspection for Team Steinhausen Racing#1, suspected modifications to camshafts relative to homologated reference parts, cancellation of all results for this event, and an appeal having been filed. This is a pre-appeal event announcement, not the final ruling.

**Evidence Link:**

https://www.fim-moto.com/en/news/news-detail/article/update-following-fim-sidecar-world-championship-round-7

**Result of this step:** Obtain the team name and FIM International Court of Appeal as the next hop.

## Step 06 · Verify the final case number and time

**Action:** Enter the official ruling CAI-2025-03 and verify the header and homepage date explanation.

**Evidence Observation:**

The ruling with reasons is dated 2026-02-04; the homepage also distinguishes a notification without reasons on January 28. The question asks for the "final ruling date," so February 4 is adopted; one cannot mix the two as the same day just because an earlier notification exists.

**Evidence Link:**

https://www.fim-moto.com/fileadmin/user_upload/Campagnes/Administration/2026/CAI-2025-03-2026-02-04-Decision_CAI_web.pdf

**Result of this step:** Case number CAI-2025-03 and ruling date are fixed.

## Step 07 · Read the submitted object and the reference item

**Action:** Locate the comparative testing section by the Department of Industrial Engineering at the University of Padua on pages 5–6 of the ruling.

**Evidence Observation:**

Yamaha homologated reference intake camshaft number 13S-12170-01 was submitted for comparison; another number, FIM000529, is the seal identifier for the inspected item. The original standard part number and the seal number serve different functions; subsequent retrieval should use the former.

**Evidence Link:**

https://www.fim-moto.com/fileadmin/user_upload/Campagnes/Administration/2026/CAI-2025-03-2026-02-04-Decision_CAI_web.pdf

**Result of this step:** Obtain the Yamaha intake camshaft number that allows entry into the parts catalogue.

## Step 08 · Read the main text of the ruling rather than guessing the result

**Action:** Turn to the conclusion on page 29 and verify the disposition of the appeal and whether the original penalty is maintained.

**Evidence Observation:**

The ruling dismisses the appeal and upholds the disqualification. One cannot carry forward the earlier pending status of "appeal filed," nor infer on one's own from the technical testing section whether the disqualification was revoked.

**Evidence Link:**

https://www.fim-moto.com/fileadmin/user_upload/Campagnes/Administration/2026/CAI-2025-03-2026-02-04-Decision_CAI_web.pdf

**Result of this step:** The result for the second question is closed; proceed to the 2014 parts diagram.

## Step 09 · Use the camshaft number to locate the vehicle model and diagram

**Action:** Example query: 13S-12170-01 2014 Yamaha parts catalogue CAMSHAFT CHAIN.

**Evidence Observation:**

Page 11 of the 2014 YZF-R6 catalogue PDF, printed page 5, is FIG.4 CAMSHAFT & CHAIN. Item 1 in the figure, 13S-12170-01, corresponds to the number in the ruling; the order format is supplemented as 13S-12170-01-00; this step connects the component in the legal case to the correct vehicle model catalogue.

**Evidence Link:**

https://www.incolmotos-yamaha.com.co/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/R6_2014.pdf
https://www.partzilla.com/catalog/yamaha/motorcycle/2014/yzfr6-yzfr6el/camshaft-chain

**Result of this step:** Lock in 2014 YZF-R6 and FIG.4.

## Step 10 · Locate the component to the right of gasket No. 7

**Action:** Compare the exploded view position with the parts list on the same page; first confirm No. 7, then trace the lead line for No. 6 to its right.

**Evidence Observation:**

No. 7 is GASKET,TENSIONER CASE, 2C0-12213-00-00; immediately to its right is No. 6, named TENSIONER ASSY,CAM CHAIN. Position reading and the number table are used jointly for identification; one must not answer with the gasket itself (No. 7) as the tensioner.

**Evidence Link:**

https://www.incolmotos-yamaha.com.co/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/R6_2014.pdf
https://www.partzilla.com/catalog/yamaha/motorcycle/2014/yzfr6-yzfr6el/camshaft-chain

**Result of this step:** The target is tensioner item No. 6 in the figure.

## Step 11 · Verify the 2014 historical tensioner number

**Action:** Read item No. 6 number in the 2014 catalogue table and cross-check with the OEM text mirror.

**Evidence Observation:**

The historical catalogue lists 13S-12210-01; the complete order format is 13S-12210-01-00. The model year constraint takes effect here: even if the current online catalogue has switched to a subsequent number, it cannot override the historical number specified in the question.

**Evidence Link:**

https://www.incolmotos-yamaha.com.co/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/R6_2014.pdf
https://www.partzilla.com/catalog/yamaha/motorcycle/2014/yzfr6-yzfr6el/camshaft-chain

**Result of this step:** Note down the 2014 number 13S-12210-01-00.

## Step 12 · Trace two early interchangeable numbers

**Action:** Example query: 13S-12210-01 interchangeable OEM parts; read the Webike field and cross-check with the Partzilla old number page.

**Evidence Observation:**

Preserve the verification column Interchangeable OEM parts as 13S-12210-00-00 and 2C0-12210-00-00; the Partzilla old 2C0 number page states it was superseded by 13S122100100. When archiving, the direct Webike download timed out; based on the retained index and official mirror fields, do not claim this as a successful re-access performed during this session.

**Evidence Link:**

https://japan.webike.net/products/24322785.html
https://www.partzilla.com/product/yamaha/2C0-12210-00-00

**Result of this step:** The relationship between the two early numbers and the 2014 number receives cross-support.

## Step 13 · Isolate the current subsequent number

**Action:** Check the supersedes field for the same vehicle model figure item No. 6 on MotoSport.

**Evidence Observation:**

The current subsequent number 13S-12210-02-00 replaces 13S-12210-01-00, indicating a catalogue version update. It is neither the 2014 number asked in the question nor one of the two early interchangeable numbers asked; retain this page to explain apparent conflicts, while the final answers to the three questions are filled strictly according to their respective timeframes.

**Evidence Link:**

https://www.motosport.com/streetbike/oem-parts/yamaha/2014/yzf_r6/camshaft-chain

**Result of this step:** Complete the layering of "original number / historical number / current number".

## Step 14 · Check evidence dependencies and answer boundaries

**Action:** Connect the obtained bridge entities in dependency order; check each question for number mismatches, timeframe shifts, or inferences written as facts.

**Evidence Observation:**

Dependency chain: track contour → FIM race documents → final appeal ruling → standard camshaft number → 2014 Yamaha exploded view → tensioner historical number and interchangeable numbers.

Boundaries to retain: The previous Webike verification timed out during direct download; the notification date and the date with reasons differ; the current -02 number does not replace the 2014 -01 number.

**Evidence links:**

Current question prompt and input attachments; this step does not introduce external web pages.

**Result of this step:** Each field adopts the evidence directly corresponding to it above; organize the confirmed conclusions according to the numbering, tables, and units specified in the question prompt.

**Action:** Submit the answer with the fields required by the current question prompt.

**Evidence observation:** Cross-checks of objects, sources, and corresponding versions have been completed; previously unconfirmable information has been retained.

**Result of this step:**

(1) Racetrack: Motorsport Arena Oschersleben; Race: Round 7 of the 2025 FIM Sidecar World Championship, IMN 105/07; Date: October 3–5, 2025.

(2) Case number: FIM International Court of Appeal CAI-2025-03; Ruling date: February 4, 2026; Result: Appeal dismissed, disqualification decision upheld; Standard camshaft brand: Yamaha; Part number: 13S-12170-01 (full order number 13S-12170-01-00).
